hero.title: One platform for your whole company.
hero.subtitle: Replace the 10 apps you adopted one at a time with one workspace that actually works together.
hero.description: Tech startups, growing agencies, professional services firms, and any company of 2–50 people drowning in tools.

section1.heading: Count your subscriptions
section1.p1: Slack for chat. Asana for tasks. Notion for documents. Google Workspace for email and calendar. HubSpot for the CRM. Calendly for scheduling. Zapier to glue them together. Loom for async video. Maybe Toggl for time tracking. Maybe Intercom for support.
section1.p2: A 9-person startup paying per-seat for all of these is looking at $4,200 a month. More than most office rents. And none of these tools talk to each other without Zapier holding them together with duct tape.

section2.heading: But the money isn't the real problem
section2.p1: The real cost is fragmentation. Your CEO spends 45 minutes every morning scanning Slack, Gmail, Asana, and the CRM just to figure out what's happening. Three messages need responses, and the context for each one lives in a different tool.
section2.p2: Your weekly team meeting is 45 minutes long, and half of it is status updates — everyone reporting what they're working on because there's no shared view. The other half generates action items that someone writes on a whiteboard. Two are forgotten by 2pm.
section2.p3: A new hire takes weeks to become productive — not because the work is hard, but because they need access to ten tools and have to learn which source of truth to check for which type of information.
section2.p4: And when the CEO asks "what's the status of the Henderson deal?" — three people check three tools and give three different answers.

section3.heading: What one platform changes
section3.briefing: "3 tasks overdue — 2 waiting on the Henderson contract review. 2 emails need your decision. Revenue this week is 12% above forecast. One team member flagged a blocker yesterday at 6pm."
section3.briefingNote: Five minutes. Full picture. Zero app switching.
section3.p1: Team meetings drop from 45 minutes to 25. A pre-meeting brief is auto-generated from actual project data. Live transcription captures everything. Action items are extracted and assigned based on role and workload. Nobody spends time on status updates — the dashboard already shows everything.
section3.p2: New employees get one login and a role-specific dashboard on day one. When they ask VOIS "what's the usual process for onboarding a new client?" — it finds the Playbook, the last three client onboarding projects, and a meeting transcript where the team discussed improvements. One question, one answer, full context.
section3.p3: When the CEO asks about the Henderson deal, there's one CRM record with one truth: deal stage, last communication, project completion, outstanding invoice, and an AI assessment — "at risk, client hasn't confirmed pricing, call today."
section3.p4: Five AI Advisors — Finance, Strategy, Operations, Marketing, Sales — offer perspectives that intentionally disagree. Because real business decisions have tradeoffs, and consensus from a single AI is just a confident guess.

testimonial.quote: "We were paying more for software subscriptions than our office rent. Slack, Notion, Asana, HubSpot, Calendly, Toggl, Google Workspace, Zapier — $4,200 a month. HABOS replaced all of them for $315. But the real win isn't the money — it's that when I ask a question about a client, I get one answer instead of three."
